paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to carry out of this one. The LORD didn't open with a scolding. He opened with a memory: "I remember the devotion of your youth, your love as a bride" (Jeremiah 2:2). That tells me how He feels about His people, even while they're walking away. He is the One who stays close, and He is the One who remembers.

Now look at the heart of it. The LORD says His people committed two evils: "They have forsaken Me, the fountain of living water, and they have dug their own cisterns" (Jeremiah 2:13). They left the source and then worked hard on something that "cannot hold water." I've baked a lot of cookies, and I can tell you that a good oven beats a lot of hard work with no heat. Whatever we lean on in place of God will run dry, no matter how much sweat we pour into it.

So here's the question for you today, baker. What are you dipping your bucket into when you're thirsty? The LORD asks His people what they will gain by drinking from the Nile or the Euphrates (Jeremiah 2:18), and He's asking us the same thing. The good news is the Fountain is still flowing. Go back to Him, and don't leave Him for a bucket full of holes.
